query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_sentiment
per_column.rationale: A review theme extracted from free text with three well-separated, human-readable categories (indifferent_rude / professional_friendly / exceptional_attentive). These form a clean ordinal-ish segmentation that can be cross-tabbed against Overall Rating within Type of Traveller and Class. It is not a bare positive/negative score but a labelled service-quality gradient, so it supports interpretable relationship discovery. Mild conceptual overlap with the existing numeric 'Staff Service' rating, but as a text-derived thematic label it still adds a distinct, groupable axis.

per_column.name: aircraft_condition_status
per_column.rationale: Captures a distinct review theme (fleet/aircraft condition) absent from the original numeric columns. Categories (modern_well_maintained / adequately_maintained / showing_age / outdated_worn) are clearly ordered and interpretable, allowing meaningful segmentation against Overall Rating. NULL share (~1709) is non-trivial but the populated categories are well distributed, so comparisons remain informative.

per_column.name: operational_reliability
per_column.rationale: Encodes a punctuality/disruption theme not represented in the original schema. The categories (reliable_on_time / minor_delay_managed / significant_delay_unmanaged / cascading_disruption) are well-separated and interpretable along a severity scale, making them ideal for segment-vs-rating comparisons. This is a genuinely external, associational variable for the focus.

per_column.name: ground_staff_professionalism
per_column.rationale: A ground-service theme distinct from in-flight staff, with four clean, interpretable categories (professional / efficient_helpful / slow_disorganized / rude_unhelpful) spanning positive to negative. Low NULL count and balanced distribution make it a strong grouping variable to compare against Overall Rating across traveller/class segments.

per_column.name: price_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Value-for-money theme with interpretable categories (premium_value_justified / fair_value / poor_overpriced / aggressive_cost_cutting) that segment cleanly. It conceptually overlaps with the existing numeric 'Value For Money' column, but as a categorical text-derived theme it offers a directly groupable qualitative axis aligned with the 'review themes' framing of the query, so it still functions as a usable predictor rather than a restatement of the focus.

judge.rationale: The query asks which REVIEW THEMES relate to higher/lower Overall Rating within Type of Traveller and Class. All five added columns are text-derived thematic variables with interpretable, well-separated categorical scales (service, aircraft condition, reliability, ground staff, price/value) rather than opaque scores or mechanical text statistics. None restates the focus (Overall Rating), and each can be grouped/segmented and cross-tabbed against it, satisfying the EDA claim of opening informative, human-understandable relationships. Slight deduction because two themes (cabin crew sentiment, price/value) conceptually echo existing numeric rating columns (Staff Service, Value For Money), and a couple carry moderate NULL rates, marginally reducing independent explanatory coverage; but as a set they strongly support interpretable relationship discovery.
